calibre: server end to end: 1e6 * B / decode tok/s (client clock over HTTP, prompt 64, 1024 new tokens, greedy; 2 server starts x 3 repeats, eval/client.py through scripts/compare.sh). Both systems were measured by the same client on one H100 each, in two jobs. The engine under test is timed in its own process (step, no sampling, no HTTP): the easier calibre, so a speedup here is an upper bound on the end-to-end one until the engine is measured behind the same client.
source: <job> (Cohere's server: 276.6 tok/s at B=1, 1114.9 at B=8) and <job> (vLLM: 198.1 / 862.3), 2026-11-10. Cohere's server streams only on its chat endpoint: its requests carry the chat template (180 prompt tokens instead of 64) and at B=8 it sends several tokens per chunk. vLLM needed --max-model-len 32768 (the model's own 500000 does not leave room for the KV cache next to 61 GB of weights). SGLang does not list this model. Earlier bring-up trial <job> (512 tokens): 286.2 / 1113.3 tok/s; Cohere's own decode-only runner: 287 / 977
